notes: Lead: CTO Marcus Li; product PM: Elena Park (owns integration)
Primary motivation: stabilize latency/variance observed on Hosted during peak flows; reduce token costs for reranking-heavy pipeline
Current stack: Node.js backend, Postgres, AWS (us-east-1 primary), SSO via Okta
Use-case detail: conversational support assistant (priority) + doc search for knowledge base + a reranking job for FAQ results
Targets: chat p99 < 300ms (ideal <200ms), sustained throughput 200 req/s for support flows, reranking batch windows up to 1k queries/min
Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to commit for predictable unit cost but wants clear modeling for reserve vs burst
Security: must integrate with company KMS (AWS KMS), audit logs retained 12 months, SSO (SAML) + SCIM provisioning
Past experiment: used Redwood Hosted API for 6 weeks; stable but p99 spikes during campaign events caused user complaints
Quote from Marcus: "We can't tolerate >1% error spike during campaigns — need graceful degradation."
POC ask (agreed): 4-week Dedicated POC with canary strategy, routing/fallback plan, SLA-like SLOs measured, cost modeling for 6/12 month commits
POC success criteria: p99 latency reduction vs Hosted by 20%+, error rate <0.5% on canary, quality parity within evaluation set (human sample)
Canary plan (technical): start 5% traffic to Dedicated pool (canary variant), monitor metrics 48h, step to 20% then 50% over 7–10 days if stable

Routing/fallback plan: primary route to dedicated-gpu-prod (us-east-1); fallback options: 1) dedicated-quantized model variant in us-east-1, 2) hosted-api fallback endpoint (region-aware) if Dedicated capacity degraded; automatic failback when health checks pass
Model variants to include in POC: base: redwood-chat-1; cost-saver: redwood-chat-1-8bit; fallback small: redwood-mini for transient overloads
Region failover: primary us-east-1 -> secondary eu-west-1 for resilience; performance/cost tradeoff documented; data residency constraints scoped per flow
Rollback criteria: sustained error rate >2% for 15 minutes, p99 latency >500ms for 10 minutes, or quality regression measured by test prompts (drop >5% on baseline intent accuracy)
Observability: need per-route token/cost breakdown, trace IDs surfaced in logs, and user-level request IDs for incident replay
Pricing conversation notes: procurement prefers a 12-month reserved commit with quarterly review; asked for committed QPS tiers and burst pricing; AE provided initial estimate (see drive deck)
Ops ask: VPC peering + strict egress allowlist; networking team to provide CIDR and peering window (open item)
Legal: Data processing addendum review requested; residency for EU customers scoped separately
